title: Robust Financial Instrument Processing
business: Financial services firms managing complex derivative portfolios.
problem: High costs associated with runtime errors in legacy systems when processing diverse, nested financial transaction types.
solution: Utilizing OCaml's algebraic data types and pattern matching to enforce exhaustive handling of transaction variants at compile-time, ensuring that every possible financial state is accounted for before execution.
steps: Define a variant type representing all possible transaction states.
Implement a module signature to abstract the processing logic.
Write a pattern matching function that covers all variant cases.
Use the compiler to verify that no transaction state is left unhandled.
Encapsulate the logic within a module to maintain clean separation of concerns.
outcome: A significant reduction in production runtime exceptions related to unhandled transaction states, leading to more predictable system behavior.
limitation: The strictness of exhaustive pattern matching can make adding new transaction types require updates across all existing match statements; check this by monitoring compiler warnings for non-exhaustive patterns.
